## 1. The row

| # | Block | Delivers | Covers | Depends on |

| 23 | 🔴 **CV-23** Contract cleanup | drop the v1 signature wrappers, `chat_normalize_channel_name`, `share_op_announce`, the `client_id` idempotency path; raise `min_build`; the drift gate re-run | AC12.9, AC12.10 | all above + one desktop release after the release train |

## 2. What to build

**Edge cases this block handles** (§Edge cases)
- A desktop build from before the release → its chat sends still work through the v1-signature wrappers for one release; after `min_build` is raised it's told to update and runs read-only.

## 3. Acceptance criteria

**AC12 — Platform**
- **AC12.9** old desktop builds send through the wrappers for one release and are told to update after `min_build`
- **AC12.10** each closed vocabulary lives in `@contracts` with a matching CHECK and passes the drift gate.

**Tests that prove them** (file · name · AC · plain English)

- `src/lib/min-build.test.ts` + `supabase/tests/chat_wrappers.test.sql` · "old builds" · proves AC12.9 · The v1 send and edit signatures convert and succeed for one release; a build below `min_build` sees the update notice and runs read-only.
- `supabase/functions/_shared/contracts/drift-gates.test.ts` (existing) · "vocabularies" · proves AC12.10 · Every closed vocabulary of §Assumptions #29 matches its CHECK.

## 4. Decisions that bind it

- **What goes** (spec row; round-3 §2.3 "Retired", #4): the v1 signatures of `chat_op_send` (`p_channel_id, p_body, p_parent_id, p_mentioned_user_ids, p_notify_channel, p_client_id, p_excerpt`) and `chat_op_edit` (`p_message_id, p_body, p_mentioned_user_ids`) that CV-2a kept as converting wrappers; `chat_normalize_channel_name(text)` (unused since CV-1); `share_op_announce(channel, on)` (replaced by `chat_op_set_announcement`, CV-15); the `client_id` idempotency path (v2 sends are idempotent on the client-minted message id; the column stays for v1 rows). One migration, `…_chat_v2_contract` (#35), as `DROP FUNCTION` statements: never edit an applied migration.
- **`min_build`:** the minimum client build is `app_settings.min_build`; a build below it shows "Update Moduo" and runs read-only (`src/lib/min-build.ts`, `readOnlyFetch`, `READ_RPCS`). The row says "raise `min_build`", while #4 says it is raised at the release and the wrappers are dropped after: **ask the orchestrator for the value and the moment**; it must be at least the first desktop build that sends only v2 signatures, and this block must not apply anywhere until one desktop release after the release train (a release step, never a local one).
- **The drift gate re-run** (AC12.10): every closed vocabulary of #29 matches its CHECK in `supabase/functions/_shared/contracts/drift-gates.test.ts`: `CHAT_MESSAGE_KINDS`, `CHAT_EVENT_TYPES`, `CHAT_CATCHUP_REASONS`, `CHAT_CATCHUP_DONE_HOW`, `CHAT_LINK_TARGETS`, `CHAT_CAPABILITIES` (with `add_emoji`), `REACTION_KEY` + `DEFAULT_QUICK_REACTIONS`, `STATUS_PRESETS`, `STATUS_CLEAR_AFTER`, `CLIENT_SURFACES`, `NOTICE_DELIVERY_KINDS`, `EMAIL_KINDS`, `RELATION_KINDS`, `ATTACHMENT_DELETED_REASONS`, `CHAT_PLAN_TIERS` / `planHasChat`. Unchanged: `CHAT_CHANNEL_KINDS`, `CHAT_NOTIFY_LEVELS`, KEYS-1's scopes. Add any pin that is missing; no zombie unions (a dead value is removed everywhere).
- **Old builds** (`src/lib/min-build.test.ts` + `supabase/tests/chat_wrappers.test.sql`): after this block the wrapper assertions flip: the v1 signatures are gone, a build below `min_build` is told to update and runs read-only, and `min-build.test.ts` still classifies every RPC the client calls (`READ_RPCS`).

Touch: `supabase/tests/chat_wrappers.test.sql`, `src/lib/min-build.test.ts`, `src/lib/min-build.ts` (only if an RPC name is retired), `drift-gates.test.ts`, `vocabularies.ts` (+ test) for dead values, `docs/testing/chat-release.md` is the `/s3` checklist (the release train's order, the conversion applied once, the connector redeployed, `min_build` raised).

## 6. From earlier blocks

All of them: every wrapper, helper and vocabulary named above exists; grep the client and the MCP connector for any remaining caller of a dropped function before you write the migration.

## 7. Watch out

- A dropped function with a caller left in an old desktop build means "function not found" for that build: that is what `min_build` is for, which is why this block waits for the release.
- **Tier 2** (migrations, RLS, contracts, moduo-mcp, src/lib/runtime*): one `/code-review high` and one security scan of the diff at the end; scan findings go only into the hand-back.
- **Migration:** stamp provisional (re-cut on apply day, chat's order kept); redefine from live bodies (`pg_get_functiondef`); re-state grants by name (`DROP` + `CREATE` resets them); re-assert the Realtime publication if you publish a table; apply only on your migration turn, then `bun run db:test chat`; never `local:reset` or `migration up` (runbook, `docs/gotchas/supabase.md`).
- **Public repo:** describe no security weakness in any file; tell the orchestrator in the hand-back.

## 8. Out of scope for this block

Anything that adds behaviour; the release train itself (`email-worker`, `unaccent`, the conversion, the connector, Supabase Pro: `specs/BUILD_ORDER.md` Chat box).
